Name: First Macedonian War and Balkan Balance of Power

Variants.Content: Seeking to expand westward into Illyria, King Philip V of Macedon signed a formal mutual-defense pact with Hannibal in 215 BC. Heavily engaged in Italy, Rome could not spare major legions; instead, Roman diplomats allied with the ferocious Aetolian League, Pergamon, and Sparta to wage proxy warfare against Philip in Greece. This ten-year Balkan conflict successfully prevented Philip from ever ferrying phalanxes to reinforce Hannibal in Italy, concluding with the Peace of Phoenice in 205 BC.
We sailed small patrol squadrons in the Adriatic, keeping the Macedonian king's transports pinned in his harbors while the Greeks hacked at his northern borders.
Our Balkan diplomacy was a triumph of geopolitical balance. With minimal Roman blood spilled, our naval squadrons and Greek allies tied down the Antigonid king, ensuring Hannibal fought alone.
